sessions.title: Opening Keynote
sessions.reason: Align Vanguard's developers, platform teams, security specialists, and leaders around GitHub's direction for AI-assisted software delivery. Identify follow-ups on governance, platform strategy, and measurable value; distinguish available capabilities from future possibilities.

sessions.title: Agentic engineering past the pilot: An enterprise playbook
sessions.reason: Compare operating models for moving agentic engineering beyond pilots. For Vanguard, focus on accountable ownership, consistent governance, and how platform teams can enable product teams without creating additional approval bottlenecks.

sessions.title: How GitHub taught Copilot to remember and when to forget
sessions.reason: For Vanguard developers and AI enablement teams: examine when accumulated context helps or harms agent performance, and how to evaluate memory and forgetting. The described Skill Forge and Copilot REM work is in development, not an assumed production capability.
sessions.room: BATS Theatre @ Fort Mason Building B, 3rd Floor
sessions.note: Tight transfer: 20 minutes, including an estimated 15-minute walk and 5-minute early arrival. Allow extra time for queues.

sessions.title: Building AI fluency at UPS
sessions.reason: Use UPS's enterprise experience to examine how leaders turn access to AI tools into practical fluency. Consider reusable enablement, community participation, and evidence of changed delivery behavior rather than license allocation alone.
sessions.note: Replaces the 11:30 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: The Low Orbit Agentic Cannon: Scaling Copilot through internal tooling
sessions.reason: Galaxy offers a financial-services perspective on scaling Copilot through internal tooling. Compare the platform investment, organizational leverage, and governance questions with Vanguard's own choices about reusable enablement.
sessions.note: Replaces the 11:30 AM and 12:30 PM recommendations on this day, including transfer time. Official guidance: arrive about 20 minutes early; seating is not guaranteed.

sessions.title: Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills
sessions.reason: For developers and platform teams: learn when to package recurring work as reusable agent skills rather than repeat prompts. Compare how to encode engineering judgment and distribute useful patterns across Vanguard teams.
sessions.note: Tight transfer: 20 minutes, including an estimated 15-minute walk and 5-minute early arrival. Allow extra time for queues.

sessions.title: The factory mindset: Agentic workflows in production
sessions.reason: Evaluate the organizational changes behind governed production agent workflows. Bring back questions for Vanguard about auditability, centralized controls, ownership, and the conditions under which agent automation should expand.
sessions.note: Replaces the 12:30 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: What does shift left mean in an agentic world?
sessions.reason: Examine how evidence and human oversight change when agents participate in software delivery. Translate the demo into design and oversight questions about reviewable changes and clear accountability in a financial-services environment.

sessions.title: Disrupting supply chain attacks: A threat framework for GitHub Actions
sessions.reason: For platform and security engineers: map CI/CD attack techniques to controls across workflows, credentials, and runner infrastructure. Use the threat framework to structure follow-up on Vanguard's secure pipeline and runner design choices.

sessions.title: Beyond "hours saved": How AMD and ING measure AI at enterprise scale
sessions.reason: Compare AMD and ING's methods for evaluating enterprise AI investment. Use the banking perspective to shape Vanguard's measurement discussion around delivery outcomes, quality, and investment choices rather than hours-saved claims alone.
sessions.note: Replaces the 2:30 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Tight transfer into the 3:30 PM session: allow 20 minutes including travel and early arrival.

sessions.title: One PM, four weeks, full compliance: How itti shipped a banking product with agents
sessions.reason: Compare a banking-product team's use of AI with human approval gates and traceability. Choose this when regulated delivery and operating controls are more important than the parallel investment-measurement discussion.
sessions.room: BATS Theatre @ Fort Mason Building B, 3rd Floor
sessions.note: Replaces the 2:30 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Tight transfer into the 3:30 PM session: allow 20 minutes including travel and early arrival.

sessions.title: PATs, rulesets, and IP allowlists: How Confluent secured GitHub Enterprise Cloud
sessions.reason: Use Confluent's experience to examine what enterprise controls cost to implement and operate. Focus on ownership, rollout friction, and the tradeoffs Vanguard teams should assess when balancing developer experience and governance.

sessions.title: Stop guessing: What 37 million pull requests reveal about AI impact
sessions.reason: Use cross-company pull-request evidence to challenge simplistic AI productivity claims. Identify measures Vanguard could examine alongside quality and risk indicators; research findings are not a forecast of Vanguard's results.
sessions.note: Replaces the 3:30 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: Security by default: a maintainer’s wishlist for GitHub Actions v2
sessions.reason: For platform engineers, security, and developer enablement: examine Actions security pitfalls and fixes, and evaluate how safer defaults affect contribution workflows. Separate the maintainer's wishlist from features that are available today.
sessions.note: Tight transfer: 20 minutes, including an estimated 15-minute walk and 5-minute early arrival. Allow extra time for queues.

sessions.title: The human side of AI: How building community drove 94% Copilot adoption
sessions.reason: Learn from another financial-services organization's community-led Copilot adoption. Explore how leadership sponsorship, storytelling, and shared practice can sustain behavior change without treating another firm's adoption rate as a target or guarantee.
sessions.room: BATS Theatre @ Fort Mason Building B, 3rd Floor
sessions.note: Replaces the 4:30 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Tight transfer into the 4:30 PM session: allow 20 minutes including travel and early arrival.

sessions.title: Beyond pass or fail: How agents verify AI-generated code
sessions.reason: For developers, quality engineers, and security teams: examine how agents gather evidence and reproduce failures beyond a passing test suite. Apply deterministic boundaries and human escalation to evaluate agent-generated changes responsibly.

sessions.title: Visa's Zero-Secrets Initiative: no hardcoded secrets, no exceptions
sessions.reason: Consider Visa's approach to policy ownership, credential-risk reduction, and prevention at enterprise scale. This is a useful peer alternative for Vanguard leaders prioritizing security governance over the model-lab outlook.
sessions.room: BATS Theatre @ Fort Mason Building B, 3rd Floor
sessions.note: Replaces the 9:00 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: The view from the labs: What's next for AI-assisted development
sessions.reason: Hear model-lab leaders' outlook on AI-assisted development and pressure-test long-term investment assumptions. Consider implications for Vanguard's skills strategy, operating model, and roadmap conversations rather than assuming forecasts are commitments.
sessions.note: Replaces the 9:00 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: Write-only code: What happens to peer review when agents write the diffs
sessions.reason: Examine the tradeoffs of moving human review upstream when agents produce code. For Vanguard, focus on preserving accountability, engineering learning, and evidence of control effectiveness; treat the speakers' approach as a discussion, not a recommendation to remove required reviews.
sessions.note: Replaces the 10:20 AM recommendation on this day, including transfer time. Tight transfer into the 10:00 AM session: allow 20 minutes including travel and early arrival.

sessions.title: Open PRs, don't merge them: Fine-grained authorization for hosted MCP servers
sessions.reason: For Vanguard platform, identity, and security teams: study a per-identity authorization pattern for hosted MCP servers. Explore how to let an agent open a pull request while keeping merge approval with a human; evaluate the pattern against your own controls.
sessions.note: Official guidance: arrive about 20 minutes early; seating is not guaranteed.

sessions.title: AI, Actions, and tooling: Coinbase's move to GitHub with data residency
sessions.reason: Study Coinbase's regulated platform migration for lessons in developer productivity, data residency, and self-service. Compare change-management and governance choices relevant to Vanguard's platform strategy without assuming the same architecture or regulatory requirements.

sessions.title: The night shift: Copilot agents that maintain their own self-hosted runners
sessions.reason: For platform and operations teams: examine policy-gated automation for maintaining self-hosted runners, updating dependencies, and escalating risky changes. Treat this as a self-hosted operating pattern, not a recommendation to choose it over hosted runners.
sessions.room: BATS Theatre @ Fort Mason Building B, 3rd Floor
sessions.note: Tight transfer: 20 minutes, including an estimated 15-minute walk and 5-minute early arrival. Allow extra time for queues.

sessions.title: 17 agents, one SDLC: How Levi Strauss reimagined development on GitHub
sessions.reason: Evaluate Levi Strauss's multi-agent software lifecycle and human approval gates. Discuss which decision rights, readiness milestones, and escalation paths Vanguard would need before applying similar patterns across product teams.
sessions.note: Replaces the 12:00 PM and 1:00 PM recommendations on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: People, process, and GitHub: Eliminating 90% of enterprise AppSec risk
sessions.reason: Use Manulife's regulated-enterprise perspective to compare security culture, risk visibility, and remediation accountability. Look for leadership practices relevant to Vanguard without assuming insurer-specific requirements or numeric outcomes transfer.
sessions.note: Replaces the 12:00 PM and 1:00 PM recommendations on this day, including transfer time. Official guidance: arrive about 20 minutes early; seating is not guaranteed.

sessions.title: Treat your AI context as infrastructure
sessions.reason: For developers, platform engineering, and enablement teams: compare instructions, skills, custom agents, and MCP as managed context infrastructure. Take away a practical approach to standardizing and distributing useful context across Vanguard teams.
sessions.note: Tight transfer: 20 minutes, including an estimated 15-minute walk and 5-minute early arrival. Allow extra time for queues.

sessions.title: Why sketching in code matters more in the age of AI
sessions.reason: Explore the role of human understanding and creative judgment as AI generates more output. Use the discussion to inform Vanguard's leadership approach to team learning, cross-functional collaboration, and accountability for technology decisions.
sessions.note: Replaces the 1:00 PM recommendation on this day, including transfer time.

sessions.title: Closing Keynote
sessions.reason: Reconvene and compare technical and leadership takeaways on responsible agents, engineering outcomes, and platform strategy for Vanguard. The detailed keynote program is still developing; no specific announcement is assumed.
sessions.note: Tight transfer: 20 minutes, including an estimated 15-minute walk and 5-minute early arrival. Allow extra time for queues.
